paper.title: Language Generation and Identification From Partial Enumeration: Tight Density Bounds and Topological Characterizations
paper.summary: Studies generation and identification from partial enumeration through tight density bounds, semi-index reductions, priority algorithms, and topological characterizations.

formalization_scope.summary: The source-centered headline inventory covers the principal semantic partial-enumeration generators, the warm-up and optimal density endpoints, and both the full- and partial-enumeration topological claims. Generation and full-text identification are complete at their documented semantic interfaces; the density theorems retain explicit missing dynamic-charge bridges, while the partial-enumeration topology remains unformalized because its pinned definition is internally inconsistent.
specializations: Languages are an explicit Nat-indexed family over natural-number strings, and partial enumeration is represented by an exact presentation of an infinite subset of the target.
The generation algorithms are semantic and may use classical choice; no finite-time membership-oracle implementation is claimed.
The full-text topology uses the paper's nonempty-language assumption and repaired exact-text reading.
gaps: Theorem 3.1 still needs a new skipped-level queue or token charge establishing coverage by the conditional warm-up certificate.
Theorem 3.5 still needs the dynamic pod construction to supply every fixed-size certificate on one output run.
The partial-enumeration intersection topology and Theorems 4.12--4.13 are registered but unformalized because the pinned source gives incompatible descriptions of its basic opens.
The paper has no Results/Overview.lean facade yet; claim links therefore point to canonical proof modules.

audit_refs.scope: Direct AI-assisted comparison of the ten headline claim groups against the SHA-256-pinned arXiv v1 PDF, including repairs, unresolved proof obligations, and the ambiguous partial-enumeration topology; no human certification is claimed.
Generated declaration-existence, defining-module, and axiom-allowlist checks for every claim-linked P15 declaration.

claim_inventory.scope_description: Ten source-centered headline groups: Overview Theorems 1.5--1.11 together with their detailed counterparts, including density Theorems 3.1 and 3.5, Theorem 4.9, Corollaries 4.10--4.11, and partial-enumeration Theorems 4.12--4.13.
exclusions: Individual Claims and Lemmas supporting Algorithms 1 and the Section 3 accounting are represented through the main-result cards rather than standalone cards.
Overview restatements are grouped with their detailed theorem rather than duplicated as separate cards.
Unnumbered prose and proof-only helper assertions are excluded.
claim_inventory.notes: Complete is relative to the paper's headline theorem surface. The ambiguous topology and its two theorems receive explicit zero-coverage cards rather than disappearing from the inventory; Lean helpers appear only as links or formalization components.

lean_declaration_inventory.scope_description: Canonical endpoints for the eight selected source claims, including conditional density endgames and the counterexample to the stronger partial-text reading.
exclusions: Proof-only finite-prefix, queue, token, and density-accounting helpers.
Duplicate equivalent endpoints when one canonical theorem already represents a selected claim.
Definitions that do not independently represent a selected numbered result.
lean_declaration_inventory.notes: Complete is relative to this first selected claim inventory, not to every declaration imported by the P15 umbrella.

claims.title: Generation from every infinite partial enumeration
claims.statement_summary: One algorithm achieves generation in the limit for every countable collection when the adversary enumerates any infinite subset of its chosen target language.

source_assessment.notes: Lean proves the existential semantic conclusion without claiming roundwise identity with the source's displayed three-case algorithm.

formalization.notes: The finite-scope selector eventually chooses an infinite intersection contained in the target and emits a fresh element.

lean_links.notes: The standing family-wide infinitude assumption is retained although the proof uses only infinitude of the presented subset.

audit_refs.scope: Generated existence, defining-module, and axiom-allowlist audit for the Theorem 2.1 endpoint; source correspondence remains AI-assisted.

claims.title: Every countable collection is conjunction-generatable from partial enumeration
claims.statement_summary: One algorithm achieves conjunction-based generation in the limit for every countable language collection under arbitrary infinite partial enumeration.

source_assessment.notes: Lean states the conjunction property directly for the semantic finite-scope selector.

formalization.notes: Lean proves the stronger invariant that every selected intersection is infinite, together with eventual target containment, for an explicit Nat-indexed family.

lean_links.notes: The selected intersection is the denotation of the returned semi-index.

relations.notes: The element generator chooses fresh points from the selected semi-index intersection.

audit_refs.scope: Generated existence, defining-module, and axiom-allowlist audit for the Overview Theorem 1.7 endpoint.

claims.title: Conjunction-based generation is accurate infinitely often
claims.statement_summary: One conjunction-based generator works for every countable collection and, at infinitely many time steps, its finite intersection contains the adversary's entire enumerated subset.

source_assessment.notes: Lean uses an uncompressed raw-index run and totalizes the early fallback, so no false round-for-round identity with the displayed compressed trace is asserted.

formalization.notes: The complete theorem-level semantic path through Lemma 2.5 and Theorems 2.2 and 2.4 is packaged by the source-facing endpoint.

lean_links.notes: Stuttering rounds preserve the theorem-level guarantee while avoiding an unsupported trace equality.

relations.notes: The concrete run realizes the semantic semi-index properties exposed by Theorem 1.7.

audit_refs.scope: Generated existence, defining-module, and axiom-allowlist audit for the Overview Theorem 1.8 endpoint.

claims.title: Warm-up generation achieves one third of input density
claims.statement_summary: The Section 3 warm-up construction is intended to convert partial-enumeration lower density alpha into generated-element lower density at least alpha/3.

source_assessment.notes: The printed latest-return charge lacks a revisit premise: changed-chain resets can skip unvisited levels, so the source does not establish coverage of every bad point by the claimed charge.

formalization.notes: The recursive priority run, eventual validity, latest-return value/rank facts, finite accounting, and alpha/3 liminf endgame are proved; the missing domain-coverage theorem is not.

components.summary: The recursive warm-up run is fresh, injective, and eventually target-valid.
A complete warm-up charge certificate implies output lower density at least alpha/3.
Every late bad enumerated point lies in the latest-return eligibility domain.

lean_links.notes: The validity proof drains every finite legacy queue rather than assuming invalid entries disappear.
This is the exact numerical endgame conditional on the certificate the dynamic proof has not yet constructed.

relations.notes: The warm-up priority execution is driven by the concrete Algorithm 1 intersections.

audit_refs.scope: Generated audit covers the conditional alpha/3 endpoint only; it does not certify the missing dynamic charge-domain coverage.

claims.title: Optimal partial-enumeration density is one half of input density
claims.statement_summary: The growing-pod construction is intended to achieve generated-element lower density at least alpha/2 from a partial enumeration of lower density alpha.

source_assessment.notes: The statement includes an extraneous universal epsilon that does not occur in its exact alpha/2 conclusion. More substantively, the proof treats an element of the cumulative pod union as if it belonged to the newly created pod; a new historical-capture invariant is needed.

formalization.notes: Correct finite four-class arithmetic and the same-run fixed-s to alpha/2 limit are proved, but the source's dynamic construction does not yet supply the required certificates.

components.summary: For each fixed pod size s, the corrected counting yields alpha/(2+4/s).
Certificates for every fixed s on one output run imply the exact alpha/2 endpoint.
The actual source run supplies the fixed-s certificates with a valid historical-capture invariant.

lean_links.notes: Corrects the extra division by s in the source's displayed finite arithmetic.
The certificate isolates the valid source-shaped numerical endgame without asserting that the dynamic pod run constructs it.

relations.notes: The optimal pod refinement improves the warm-up alpha/3 factor to alpha/2.

audit_refs.scope: Generated audit covers the quantifier-correct alpha/2 endgame only; it does not certify the missing dynamic pod bridge.

claims.title: Full-text identification is characterized by countability and the TD condition
claims.statement_summary: For a countable underlying string universe, identification in the Gold-Angluin full-enumeration model is possible exactly when the language class is countable and the paper's full-enumeration topology is TD.

source_assessment.notes: The theorem statement matches the countability-plus-TD characterization. Lean derives countability from successful identification and uses the intended reading of the malformed supporting tell-tale display in Theorem 4.8.

formalization.notes: The complete semantic/full-text equivalence reuses the extensional Angluin characterization and the paper-local topology.

lean_links.notes: The forward direction proves countability; the reverse direction uses the repaired finite tell-tale condition.

relations.notes: The proof reuses the earlier extensional tell-tale characterization.

audit_refs.scope: Generated existence, defining-module, and axiom-allowlist audit for the full-text Theorem 4.9 endpoint.

claims.title: Separation in the limit is characterized by the T1 condition
claims.statement_summary: With separation defined using every adversarial enumeration whose range may be only a subset of the target, a language collection is separated in the limit if and only if the paper's topology is T1.

source_assessment.notes: The printed arbitrary partial-text reading is false; Lean proves an exact-full-text special case and supplies a two-language counterexample to the stronger reading. The card remains partial to keep both source components visible.

formalization.notes: The repaired exact-full-text theorem and a kernel-checked refutation of the stronger possibly-subset reading are both registered; the literal stronger claim is not assigned full coverage.

components.summary: Separation from exact full texts is equivalent to the T1 condition.
The same equivalence for every infinite text whose range may be only a subset of the target.

lean_links.notes: This is the well-posed reading used by the source proof.
The counterexample has two incomparable infinite candidates and an infinite common observed language.

relations.notes: T1 implies TD, so exact-text separation yields the identification condition.

audit_refs.scope: Generated audits cover both the repaired Corollary 4.10 endpoint and the explicit counterexample to the stronger reading.

claims.title: Exact-full-text separation is equivalent to an inclusion antichain
claims.statement_summary: A nonempty-language class is separable from exact full texts exactly when no two distinct class languages are comparable by inclusion.

source_assessment.notes: Unlike Corollary 4.10, this corollary explicitly assumes the full-enumeration model, so its inclusion-antichain statement does not require a source repair.

formalization.notes: The antichain characterization follows directly from the finite-history exact-text separation interface.

lean_links.notes: The source already restricts this corollary to full enumeration; the Lean theorem states that exact-text result directly.

relations.notes: It follows from the valid exact-full-text component of Corollary 4.10 because the paper-local T1 condition is equivalent to the inclusion-antichain property.

audit_refs.scope: Generated existence, defining-module, and axiom-allowlist audit for the exact-full-text Corollary 4.11 endpoint.

claims.title: Partial-enumeration identification is characterized by TD Kolmogorov quotients
claims.statement_summary: Identification in the limit from every infinite partial enumeration is claimed to hold exactly when, for every target language L and every infinite subset C of L, the Kolmogorov quotient of the associated space tau_C is a TD space.

source_assessment.notes: The pinned source gives incompatible descriptions of the tau_C basic opens: the surrounding text alternates between conditions indexed by some relevant C and by every C while calling the result the coarsest topology. The theorem cannot be assigned one faithful Lean statement without first choosing or repairing that definition.

formalization.notes: No Lean topology or theorem is provided because the pinned source does not determine a unique tau_C interface.

relations.notes: The full-enumeration TD characterization is the unambiguous special regime; the partial-enumeration claim replaces it by a family of Kolmogorov quotients.

audit_refs.scope: Source wording and the incompatible tau_C descriptions were compared directly against the pinned arXiv v1 PDF; no Lean declaration is claimed.

claims.title: Partial-enumeration identification is invariant under finite deletion
claims.statement_summary: Deleting a finite set of ground strings from every language, and then identifying duplicates, is claimed to preserve and reflect identifiability in the partial-enumeration model.

source_assessment.notes: The proof is routed through Theorem 4.12 and the same ambiguously specified tau_C topology. The finite-deletion statement is mathematically plausible, but the pinned proof does not provide an interpretation-independent theorem to formalize.

formalization.notes: No Lean theorem is registered until the source's partial-enumeration topology and Theorem 4.12 are disambiguated.

relations.notes: The printed proof invokes the TD characterization of every tau_C Kolmogorov quotient.

audit_refs.scope: Statement and proof dependency were compared directly against the pinned arXiv v1 PDF; no Lean declaration is claimed.
